After breakfast, head to Los Cardones National Park. Set high in the mountains, the park is known for its enormous cacti, some of which are 200 to 300 years old.

Your guide will share local legends and explain the region’s high-altitude ecology. The road passes through arid landscapes dotted with giant cardón cacti. There are stops along the way to rest, take photographs and buy local souvenirs. Return to Salta after the visit.
Salta Cathedral and its two towers illuminated at dusk, Argentina
Salta: the illuminated cathedral façade behind the trees of the square

Leave Salta in the morning. The drive to Purmamarca takes about four hours. The highlights of the day are the Hill of Seven Colours and the Quebrada de Humahuaca.

The Quebrada de Humahuaca is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its natural landscapes and a cultural history stretching back more than 10,000 years. For centuries this route linked settlements in the Andes. Indigenous fortresses, prehistoric caves, farmsteads, and pre-Columbian and colonial settlements survive in the gorge. Colourful rock formations sit alongside small towns, churches and traces of ancient cultures.

In Purmamarca, see the Hill of Seven Colours and the historic Church of Santa Rosa de Lima. Continue to Tilcara, the site of an old Indigenous fortification.

On the way, visit Uquía and its church, which houses the celebrated paintings of angels with arquebuses. Continue to Humahuaca on the banks of the Río Grande, where you can walk along narrow cobbled streets and see colonial-era monuments.
